title: Column overhead purity deteriorates
scenario: A distillation column that normally meets overhead product specification begins showing poorer overhead purity. Feed rate is approximately unchanged and no major operator intervention has been reported.
expected_reasoning: Do not assume a single cause from product composition alone.
Check feed composition and thermal condition, reflux flow/temperature, reboiler duty, column pressure, condenser performance, and key tray temperatures.
Validate analyzer and flow/temperature measurements before relying on them.
Use the temperature/composition profile and recent trends to distinguish separation loss from bad measurement or feed change.
critical_errors: Immediately increasing heat or reflux without checking constraints or evidence.
Declaring flooding, weeping, or fouling as fact without supporting data.
expert_questions: Did feed composition or feed temperature change?
What happened to reflux ratio and condenser approach?
Did column pressure or differential pressure change?
Do tray-temperature trends support the analyzer result?

title: Heat exchanger duty declines
scenario: A shell-and-tube exchanger shows declining outlet temperature performance over several weeks while the nominal inlet temperatures appear stable.
expected_reasoning: Consider fouling but also verify process and utility flow rates, temperature measurements, phase behavior, bypass leakage, control-valve behavior, and pressure drop.
Trend UA or an equivalent normalized performance indicator if sufficient data exist.
Compare process-side and utility-side pressure-drop trends to localize degradation.
critical_errors: Calling the exchanger fouled solely because duty declined.
Recommending cleaning before validating measurements and operating conditions.
expert_questions: Have both-side flow rates remained constant?
How have pressure drops changed?
Has utility supply pressure/temperature changed?
Is there any bypass or control-valve leakage?

title: Centrifugal compressor discharge pressure falls
scenario: A centrifugal compressor's discharge pressure decreases relative to normal operation. Suction pressure is reported as roughly stable, but throughput is also changing.
expected_reasoning: Separate machine performance from system resistance and measurement effects.
Review suction temperature/composition, speed, recycle position, guide-vane position if applicable, discharge-system pressure, and compressor-map position.
Check whether the apparent pressure loss is expected from the new operating point.
critical_errors: Assuming mechanical damage without checking process conditions.
Suggesting operation beyond established compressor or surge-control limits.
expert_questions: What changed first: throughput, discharge pressure, or recycle?
Did gas molecular weight or suction temperature change?
Where is the operating point relative to the validated compressor map?
Are speed and anti-surge measurements trustworthy?

title: Pump vibration increases
scenario: A centrifugal pump develops elevated vibration and reduced discharge pressure. The suction vessel level is lower than usual but still above the nominal low-level alarm.
expected_reasoning: Consider suction limitations/cavitation, gas entrainment, hydraulic operating point, mechanical condition, and instrument validity.
Check suction pressure, temperature, NPSH margin where available, strainer differential pressure, valve lineup, and vibration character.
Do not infer adequate suction conditions merely because vessel level is above an alarm.
critical_errors: Continuing to push the pump harder without checking suction conditions.
Equating one alarm threshold with guaranteed adequate NPSH.
expert_questions: What is suction pressure at the pump?
Has fluid temperature or composition changed?
Is strainer or suction-line pressure drop elevated?
Did the vibration spectrum or sound change?

title: Dehydration bed outlet moisture rises early
scenario: A cyclic adsorption dehydration system begins showing moisture breakthrough significantly earlier than its historical cycle length.
expected_reasoning: Consider regeneration effectiveness, inlet water loading, flow distribution/channeling, adsorbent degradation, switching-valve leakage, analyzer validity, and temperature profile.
Use regeneration temperature/time and bed temperature-profile history to separate capacity loss from regeneration or distribution problems.
Check whether inlet conditions increased the water load before concluding the adsorbent is spent.
critical_errors: Declaring the desiccant exhausted without evaluating regeneration and loading.
Ignoring analyzer validation when the change is abrupt.
expert_questions: Did regeneration temperature and duration reach normal targets?
Has feed water loading or gas rate changed?
Did the bed temperature profile change?
Could a switching valve be leaking?

title: Level loop begins oscillating
scenario: A vessel level-control loop that was historically stable develops sustained oscillation after maintenance work nearby.
expected_reasoning: Distinguish process disturbance, measurement problem, valve behavior, and tuning issue.
Check transmitter signal quality, valve stiction/deadband, controller mode/tuning, upstream cyclic disturbance, and recent configuration changes.
Prefer evidence from trends and valve position versus process response.
critical_errors: Retuning immediately without checking valve and measurement health.
Assuming oscillation is purely a controller-tuning problem.
expert_questions: Was the valve or transmitter touched during maintenance?
Does valve position move smoothly?
Is the oscillation present in upstream variables?
Were controller parameters or scaling changed?

title: Steam-user performance degrades
scenario: Several steam-heated users in one area show weaker performance during a high-demand period.
expected_reasoning: Look for a common utility limitation before diagnosing each exchanger independently.
Check steam-header pressure, condensate backpressure, trap behavior, control-valve position, and demand changes.
Use common-cause reasoning across affected users.
critical_errors: Independently blaming fouling in every affected exchanger.
Ignoring condensate-system limitations.
expert_questions: Is the steam header pressure lower than normal?
Did condensate return pressure rise?
Are affected users on the same header?
What changed in total steam demand?

title: Evaluate loss-of-flow deviation
scenario: During a HAZOP-style review of a continuously fed process vessel, the team considers the deviation 'No Flow' on a feed stream.
expected_reasoning: Identify multiple credible causes such as valve closure, upstream trip, blockage, controller/instrument failure, or loss of driving force.
Separate causes from consequences and safeguards.
Ask what the feed does chemically and thermally before judging consequence severity.
Recognize that adequacy of safeguards depends on independence, reliability, response time, and site-specific design.
critical_errors: Treating an alarm as automatically equivalent to an independent protection layer.
Inventing consequences without understanding the feed's process function.
expert_questions: What is the feed's role in heat release, dilution, reaction control, or inventory balance?
What automatic actions occur on low/no flow?
Which safeguards are independent of the initiating cause?

title: Apparent material-balance loss
scenario: A unit's daily material balance shows a persistent 3–4% unaccounted loss after a recent metering change.
expected_reasoning: Treat measurement reconciliation as a leading hypothesis because the discrepancy began after metering work.
Check meter basis, density/temperature compensation, units, calibration, totalization timing, inventory changes, flare/vent accounting, and unmeasured streams.
Quantify uncertainty before declaring a real process loss.
critical_errors: Calling the difference a leak solely from the balance.
Ignoring inventory accumulation/depletion and meter basis.
expert_questions: Were meter units or compensation settings changed?
Are beginning/end inventories included consistently?
Are all vent, flare, recycle, and drain streams accounted for?
Is the discrepancy outside expected measurement uncertainty?

title: Startup temperature deviates from expected profile
scenario: During startup, a key process temperature rises faster than the historical startup profile while several upstream conditions are still stabilizing.
expected_reasoning: Prioritize confirmation of operating limits, measurement validity, and the relationship to heat input, flow, composition, and pressure.
Compare against approved startup procedures and historical trends rather than improvising solely from model knowledge.
Recommend escalation or hold points when the cause is uncertain and consequence could be significant.
critical_errors: Recommending continued escalation of heat/input despite an unexplained abnormal temperature trend.
Substituting generic AI advice for site startup procedures or operating limits.
expert_questions: How close is the temperature to an operating or procedural limit?
Is the temperature measurement validated by another indication?
Did heat input, flow, pressure, or composition change?
What does the approved startup procedure require at this point?
